# GOM Haddock Numbers at age


**Description**: 

Historical numbers at age (mean) of Gulf of Maine haddock.  Depending on 
the timing of the most recent stock assessment, these contain a mix of 
assessment estimates and a "bridge" to current regulatory year. The bridging is
performed in a manner consistent with the stock projections, but may be updated with
realized commercial and recreational removals. 

Simulated future numbers at age for Gulf of Maine Haddock

GOM Haddock Cod has 9 age classes (Age 1 to Age 8 and Age 9+).

**Years available**: 

Mean historical numbers at age are provided for the most recent 3 years.  

Projected numbers at age are provided for the upcoming management year.


## Methods

### Data sources

For 2026, use the [2024 Management Track stock assessment](https://apps-st.fisheries.noaa.gov/sis/docServlet?fileAction=download&fileId=9882).


For 2027, these data were derived from the [2026 Management Track stock assessment](https://apps-nefsc.fisheries.noaa.gov/saw/sasi_files.php?year=2026&species_id=5&stock_id=2&review_type_id=6&info_type_id=-1&map_type_id=&filename=Gulf_of_Maine_Haddock_SAR_2026.pdf).  We used the following assumptions for fishing mortality: 0.75Fmsy (2027-2029), Constant at 2029 level (2030-2031)


### Data extraction 

Inputs need for stock assessment were obtained from stock assessment scientists. 
This includes the "WHAM" model file weight-at-age excel file.

### Data analysis/Processing

[Current Data processing code](https://github.com/kimberly-bastille/groundfishRDM/blob/main/Code/pre_sim/process_haddock_assessment_data.R) can be seen in the groundfishRDM repository. 

For 2026: 
1.  We use the actual catch (in mt) for 2023 and 2024. We use 75%FMSY for 2025-2026 mortality.
2.  We project the stock forward and extract mean NAA through 2025.
3.  We simulate 500 draws of the Numbers-at-Age for each age class for 2026 based on 
the mean and standard deviations from WHAM.

For 2027: 
1.  We use the stock assessment projections as they are provided to fishery managers.  
2.  We extract mean NAA through 2026.
3.  We simulate 500 draws of the Numbers-at-Age for each age class for 2027 based on 
the mean and standard deviations from WHAM.
